stories.headline: Analog Devices nears $1.5B all-cash deal for AI power-chip startup Empower Semiconductor

key_facts.fact: Analog Devices is in advanced talks to acquire Empower Semiconductor for approximately $1.5 billion in cash, with an announcement possible as early as Tuesday.
Empower designs integrated voltage regulator ICs (the Crescendo family) that sit directly under GPUs and other AI accelerators, delivering more than 3,000 amps to AI processors.

The deal would extend Analog Devices' acquisition streak — the company has done 16 acquisitions over the past decade, including the $20.9B Maxim Integrated takeout in 2021 and Flex Logix in November 2024.
Empower's solutions are already deployed in high-performance computing environments, and the acquisition aligns with ADI's push into AI infrastructure power management.

stories.headline: Anthropic Acquires Stainless, Reportedly Over $300M, to Pull SDK Tooling From Rival Labs

key_facts.fact: Anthropic announced on May 18, 2026 it has acquired Stainless, the dev-tools startup whose software generates SDKs for Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Cloudflare, Replicate and Runway.
Terms were not disclosed, but The Information previously reported Anthropic was in talks to buy Stainless for more than $300 million.
Anthropic told TechCrunch it will wind down all hosted Stainless products including the SDK generator; existing customers keep rights to SDKs already generated.
Stainless was founded in 2022 by former Stripe engineer Alex Rattray and is backed by Sequoia Capital and Andreessen Horowitz.
Stainless turns API specs into native SDKs across TypeScript, Python, Go, Java, Kotlin and other languages, plus MCP server tooling.

stories.headline: Blackstone Commits $5B to Build Google TPU Cloud Joint Venture, First 500MW by 2027

key_facts.fact: Blackstone announced on May 18, 2026 a US-based joint venture with Google to offer Google Cloud's Tensor Processing Units as a compute-as-a-service alternative outside Google Cloud.
Blackstone is making an initial $5 billion equity commitment with plans for the first 500 MW of capacity online in 2027.
Total investment, including leverage, could eventually reach $25 billion according to people familiar with the matter; Blackstone will hold a majority stake.
The venture will be led by Benjamin Treynor Sloss, a Google executive of more than two decades building Google infrastructure.
Google's TPU client base already includes Anthropic, Meta, and Citadel Securities; the deal underscores Google's push to loosen Nvidia's grip on AI hardware.

stories.headline: Cursor Ships Composer 2.5 Coding Model on Kimi K2.5, Pricing Holds at $0.50/$2.50 per M Tokens

key_facts.fact: Cursor released Composer 2.5 on May 18, 2026, built on the same Moonshot Kimi K2.5 open-source checkpoint as Composer 2 with continued pretraining.
Pricing held at $0.50/M input and $2.50/M output tokens; the faster variant at the same intelligence is $3.00/M input and $15.00/M output.
Composer 2.5 was trained on 25x more synthetic tasks than Composer 2, including exercises where Cursor deletes a feature and the model rebuilds it until tests pass.
Cursor put about 85% of training compute into post-training and reinforcement learning rather than the base model.
Composer 2.5 includes double usage limits during the first week of launch and is now the default model in Cursor's picker.

stories.headline: Intel pushes US/China/Taiwan PC makers to use more 18A CPUs amid AI-driven supply crunch

key_facts.fact: Intel is asking leading PC partners in the US, China and Taiwan to increase use of CPUs built with its 18A process, citing better supply than older-node chips, Nikkei Asia reported.
Intel specifically cited better supply on its Panther Lake and Wildcat Lake CPU lines, which run on 18A, versus older-node parts.
CEO Lip-Bu Tan said separately on Monday that Intel expects 'multiple' external foundry customer commitments in the second half of the year, with 18A improvements drawing growing customer interest.
Intel has built a new 18A plant in Arizona, while a separate Ohio project has faced major delays and is not expected to start production until at least 2030.

stories.headline: Iran unveils 'Hormuz Safe' Bitcoin-backed shipping insurance for Strait of Hormuz

key_facts.fact: Iran's Ministry of Economy has launched 'Hormuz Safe,' a digital insurance platform that issues marine insurance policies for vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz with payments settled in Bitcoin, per Fars News Agency reporting on May 18.
Officials project the platform could generate more than $10 billion in revenue for Iran.
Policies would cover risks such as cargo inspection, detention, and confiscation — but exclude damages from weapon strikes.
About 20% of the world's crude oil and LNG supplies flowed through Hormuz before the US-Iran war began Feb. 28, 2026; the strait has been mostly closed since.
Any use of Hormuz Safe would create sanctions-compliance risk for shipowners, traders and insurers because payments would flow to Iranian state-linked entities.

Separately, Arkham reported Iran's largest crypto exchange Nobitex has processed more than $2.3 billion since 2023 via Tron and BNB Chain, including over $23 million since the Iran war started in February.

organizations: Iran Ministry of Economy and Financial Affairs

stories.headline: Kia to deploy Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoid first in Georgia assembly plants

key_facts.fact: Kia President Song Ho-sung said on Monday during overseas non-deal roadshow meetings in Singapore and Hong Kong that the company plans to deploy Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoid robot first in difficult and physically demanding assembly processes.
Atlas will be deployed first at Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America in Georgia, and a year later at Kia's Georgia plant, because the production systems and factory structures are the same.

Hyundai Motor Group is building a humanoid mass production system with annual capacity of 30,000 units by 2028, with deployments at Hyundai Metaplant America starting in 2028 and at Kia's Georgia plant in 2029.
The disclosure also raised speculation about a potential IPO for Boston Dynamics, the US robotics company owned by Hyundai Motor Group.

stories.headline: Italy's Lexroom Raises $50M Series B for Civil-Law Legal AI, Eight Months After Series A

key_facts.fact: Milan-based Lexroom announced a $50 million / €42.9 million Series B led by Left Lane Capital, bringing total funding to about $73 million / €62.7 million.
Lexroom is now used by more than 8,000 law firms and corporate legal teams, with a product built on a proprietary database of over six million verified legal sources.
The capital will fund expansion into Spain and Germany, positioning Lexroom against US-trained, common-law-anchored legal AI rivals.
Lexroom was founded in 2023 by Paolo Fois, Martina Domenicali and Andrea Lonza; the company argues legal AI should be built from the data layer up, not by fine-tuning generalist LLMs.

stories.headline: Meta to lay off ~8,000 on May 20 while reassigning 7,000 employees into four new AI units

key_facts.fact: Meta will lay off about 10% of its workforce — roughly 8,000 employees — starting May 20, 2026, while also scrapping plans to fill 6,000 open roles.
Meta also told employees on Monday May 18 that about 7,000 workers would be reassigned to four newly created AI organizations, per an internal NYT-reported memo.
The new AI units are Applied AI Engineering (autonomous AI agents), Agent Transformation Accelerator, Central Analytics, and Enterprise Solutions.
Meta raised its 2026 capital expenditure guidance by up to $10 billion, taking the total to as high as $145 billion, largely directed at AI infrastructure.
Meta is eliminating thousands of managerial roles and instructing North American employees to work remotely on May 20, the day layoffs are scheduled.
Almost 110,000 layoffs have occurred at 137 tech companies so far in 2026, per Layoffs.fyi.

stories.headline: Jury Unanimously Rejects Musk's $150B Lawsuit Against OpenAI After Two-Hour Deliberation

key_facts.fact: A nine-person California jury unanimously rejected Elon Musk's claims against OpenAI and Sam Altman on May 18, 2026, finding the suit fell outside the statute of limitations.
Jurors deliberated about two hours after a three-week trial that included testimony from Musk, Altman, Greg Brockman and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella.
Musk had sought $150 billion in damages and Altman's removal; the verdict removes a major obstacle to OpenAI's planned IPO at an $852B valuation.
Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers accepted the advisory jury's verdict and dismissed the claims; Musk's separate claims against Microsoft were dismissed as a matter of law.
Musk's lawyer William Savitt said the jury 'decided that Musk was lying during his testimony about the company's origins'; Musk said he will appeal to the Ninth Circuit.

stories.headline: NextEra to buy Dominion for $67B in largest US utility deal, citing AI power demand

key_facts.fact: NextEra Energy agreed to acquire Dominion Energy in an all-stock deal valued at about $67 billion, the largest power acquisition in US history, creating the world's largest regulated electric utility.

NextEra shareholders will own about 74.5% of the combined company; Dominion shareholders 25.5%. The merged utility will serve about 10 million customers across Florida, Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina.

NextEra and Dominion together have roughly 130 GW of contracted data-center demand seeking grid connection, with Dominion alone holding nearly 51 GW of contracted data-center capacity from Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta.
The companies pledged $2.25 billion in customer credits over two years to Dominion ratepayers in Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina as part of the deal.
US utilities and grid operators are expected to invest more than $1.1 trillion over the next five years on new generation and transmission projects.
The deal is expected to close in mid-to-late 2027 (12-18 months).

stories.headline: Seagate plunges nearly 7% as CEO rules out new factories, drags memory chip stocks down

key_facts.fact: Seagate shares closed down about 6.9% on Monday, leading a sector-wide sell-off, after CEO Dave Mosley said at the JPMorgan Global Technology, Media and Communications Conference that building new factories would 'take too long.'
Mosley said critical components like recording head wafers have lead times exceeding nine months, with drives taking an additional quarter, and that demand 'significantly exceeds' current supply.
The sell-off extended across memory peers Micron, SanDisk and Western Digital, as well as Power Integrations and FormFactor.

Seagate is targeting mid-20s percent CAGR by advancing from 3 TB-per-platter to 4 and 5 TB-per-platter products rather than greenfield capacity additions, with Q3 non-GAAP gross margin hitting an all-time high of 47.0%.
Seagate has moved to a build-to-order model and currently provides customers with four to five quarters of forward visibility on supply.

stories.headline: Standard Chartered to cut ~7,800 back-office roles by 2030 as it scales AI automation

key_facts.fact: Standard Chartered announced on May 18, 2026, that it will cut more than 15% of its corporate functions roles — about 7,800 jobs — by 2030 as it deploys AI and automation.
The cuts target back-office functions including HR, risk, compliance and supply chain; about 52,000 of StanChart's roughly 82,000 employees work in support roles per the 2025 annual report.
CEO Bill Winters framed the reductions as 'replacing, in some cases, lower-value human capital with the financial capital and investment capital we're putting in.'
The bank aims to raise income per employee by about 20% by 2028 and target a 15% return on tangible equity in 2028, rising to roughly 18% by 2030.
StanChart has major back-office operations in India, China, Malaysia and Poland; the company said it would try to redeploy some affected workers.
The announcement was made at the bank's investor day in Hong Kong as part of CEO Bill Winters' new strategic plan.

stories.headline: Strategy buys 24,869 BTC for $2.01B, total stash hits 843,738 coins worth ~$65B

key_facts.fact: Strategy (MSTR) disclosed in a May 18 SEC 8-K filing that it bought 24,869 bitcoin between May 11 and 17 for about $2.01 billion at an average price of $80,985 per coin.
The acquisition brings Strategy's total holdings to 843,738 BTC, acquired for about $63.87 billion at an average cost basis of $75,700 per coin.
The purchases were funded almost entirely by selling 19.5 million shares of the company's high-yielding STRC preferred stock, raising about $1.9 billion, plus $84 million in common stock.
The buy comes weeks after chairman Michael Saylor said on the company's early-May earnings call that Strategy will 'probably sell some bitcoin.'
The acquisition marks a sharp escalation from Strategy's previous disclosed buy of just 535 BTC worth about $43 million earlier in May.

stories.headline: Tenstorrent draws early takeover interest from Intel and Qualcomm at $5B+ valuation

key_facts.fact: AI chip designer Tenstorrent has held early-stage takeover conversations with industry players including Intel and Qualcomm, according to Bloomberg sources.
Tenstorrent could be valued at more than $5 billion in a potential deal.
Tenstorrent, led by veteran chip designer Jim Keller, was raising $800m at a $3.2bn pre-money valuation in November 2025, up from a $693m Series D closed in December 2024 at $2.6bn.

The company designs RISC-V-based AI accelerators (Ascalon CPU cores and Tensix AI cores) sold both as packaged silicon and as licensable IP — a hybrid model that distinguishes it from pure chip startups.
Existing Tenstorrent investors include Bezos Expeditions, LG Electronics, Baillie Gifford, Hyundai Motor Group, Samsung Securities, AFW Partners, Fidelity, and the Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan.

stories.headline: Trump postpones planned Tuesday Iran attack at request of Saudi, UAE, Qatar leaders

key_facts.fact: President Trump said on May 18 he was 'holding off' a scheduled Tuesday attack on Iran after the leaders of Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Qatar asked for a pause to allow negotiations.
Trump instructed Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine to be ready for a 'full, large scale assault of Iran, on a moment's notice' if no acceptable deal is reached.
Iran on May 18 conveyed its response to Washington's latest proposal through mediator Pakistan, per Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei.
Washington's five-point proposal reportedly demands Iran keep only one nuclear site operational and transfer its highly enriched uranium stockpile to the US.
Brent crude rose more than 2% to settle at $112.10 a barrel on May 18, while WTI rose ~3% to $108.66, before easing in extended trading on news of the postponement.
The IEA warned global oil inventories are 'depleting at a record pace' with cumulative supply losses from Gulf producers already exceeding 1 billion barrels and more than 14 mb/d shut in.

stories.headline: Vatican Sets May 25 Release of Pope Leo's First Encyclical on AI, With Anthropic's Olah on Stage

key_facts.fact: The Vatican announced on May 18, 2026 that Pope Leo XIV will release his first encyclical, Magnifica Humanitas, on May 25 covering the protection of human dignity in the age of AI.
Anthropic co-founder Christopher Olah will join the pope, Curial cardinals and theologians at the May 25 presentation in the Vatican's Synod Hall.
Leo signed the encyclical on May 15, 135 years to the day after Leo XIII signed Rerum Novarum on workers' rights during the Industrial Revolution.
Speakers include Cardinal Victor Manuel Fernandez, Cardinal Michael Czerny, Professor Anna Rowlands of Durham, Olah, and Professor Leocadie Lushombo of Santa Clara University.
On May 16 the Vatican announced the creation of a cross-dicasteries AI study group covering Holy See policies on AI use.

organizations: Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith
